{"description":"The launch path serves a binary built with the release profile, and the rebuild is a deliberate act rather than a per-launch consequence of a source change.

WHAT IT MUST DO: serve release to a session; rebuild only when the builder asks; leave the edit-compile loop on debug, so an ordinary source edit never triggers the 33-minute librocksdb-sys C++ compile; and say which profile is being served, so a cost number measured in a session can be attributed to the right binary. Consumers who install a prebuilt binary through the one-liner never build at all and are already on release.

WHY IT IS FIRST: measured 2026-09-11 on the same bytes, same path, profile the only difference — a propagate walk 5,851 ms → 62 ms warm (93x), design_regions 12.5 s → 2.0 s warm. It needs no design work, and every other performance number in the 2026-09-10/11 sweep was taken on the debug binary, so nothing else in that backlog can be judged until this lands.

WHAT IT DOES NOT CLAIM: that the profile is the whole cost. The adjacency memo serving one caller while 142 edge reads still go to the store is a separate, unattributed waste.","name":"The server a session talks to is a release-profile binary, rebuilt on the builder's word rather than on every launch","provenance":"authored","status":"verified","tier":"operational"}
